thread.title: Apple To Use Foreign Profits To Fund U.S. Jobs, Manufacturing

title: Apple To Use Foreign Profits To Fund U.S. Jobs, Manufacturing
text:
Apple To Use Foreign Profits To Fund U.S. Jobs, Manufacturing January 17, 2018, 03:36:41 PM EDT By PATRICK SEITZ, Investor's Business Daily Shutterstock photo 
Consumer electronics giant Apple ( AAPL ) waved the American flag on Wednesday, pledging to contribute more than $350 billion to the U.S. economy over the next five years. 
In a press release Wednesday , the Cupertino, Calif.-based company announced a new set of investments to build on its commitment to support the U.S. economy and its workforce. Last year, Apple set up a $1 billion Advanced Manufacturing Fund to make component purchases from U.S. companies. Recipients of that funding have included Corning ( GLW ) and Finisar ( FNSR ). 
Apple is expanding its Advanced Manufacturing Fund to $5 billion and plans to create 20,000 new jobs at Apple over the next five years, the company said. Apple already employs 84,000 people in all 50 states. 
The tech icon also expects to invest over $30 billion in capital expenditures in the U.S. over the next five years, including the establishment of an Apple campus in a new location. The new campus will initially house technical support for customers. The location for the facility will be announced later this year. 
"We believe deeply in the power of American ingenuity, and we are focusing our investments in areas where we can have a direct impact on job creation and job preparedness," Apple Chief Executive Tim Cook said in a written statement. "We have a deep sense of responsibility to give back to our country and the people who help make our success possible." 
Apple's new investments add to the company's current pace of spending with domestic suppliers and manufacturers, estimated at $55 billion in 2018. Apple's spending will be aided by the repatriation of billions of dollars in foreign profits, thanks to recent U.S. tax reform. 
Apple anticipates making repatriation tax payments of about $38 billion. That implies that Apple will be bringing to the U.S. all of its $252 billion of overseas cash, Wells Fargo analyst Aaron Rakers said in a note to clients. 
IBD'S TAKE: Apple stock has an IBD Composite Rating of 90 out of a best-possible 99. For more analysis on Apple, visit the IBD Stock Checkup . 
Under legislation approved by U.S. lawmakers in December, U.S. companies may repatriate overseas cash at a 15.5% tax rate compared with the standard 35% rate. 
Apple is likely to use some of the repatriated cash to boost its returns to shareholders through increased buybacks and dividends, Rakers said. 
"We believe this sets the table for a capital allocation update on the company's upcoming fiscal first-quarter earnings call," scheduled for Feb. 1, he said. 
Apple's investments will be focused on three areas: direct employment by Apple, spending and investment with Apple's domestic suppliers and manufacturers, and fueling the app economy which Apple created with iPhone and the App Store. 
Over $10 billion of Apple's expanded capital expenditures will be for investments in data centers across the country, the company said. It currently has data centers and co-located facilities in seven states. 
Apple shares were up 1.5%, near 179, in afternoon trading on the stock market today .
